description: Frozen gate of the memory evals (#225, switched to the reranked pipeline by #226). It gates only what the phase PRD gates (recall@pool, nDCG and the correct-empty rate) and applies only to a complete run of the variant named in `variant`, which is the deployed retrieval pipeline. A slice that deploys another pipeline switches `variant` to it in the same change. Later slices may only raise the minimums, never loosen them; every other metric is reported, not gated.
method: Both baselines ran on 2026-11-21 over the complete question set (45 measured cases) with the fictional demo seed, the fictional dataset documents and the settings recorded in each summary: voyage-4, candidate pool 30, 6 final passages, relevance floor 0.3.
The minimums are the vector baseline's values rounded down to two decimals: recall@pool 1, nDCG 0.9, correct-empty rate 0.2.

MRR, hit rate, precision, the false-empty rate, provenance accuracy, latency and cost per query are reported in every summary but not gated: the PRD gates only recall@pool, nDCG and correct-empty, and the cached vector runs measure latency and cost a paid reranker cannot match.

The gate applies to the deployed variant only; a run of another variant reports the gate as not applying. Switching `variant` to a newly deployed pipeline keeps these minimums, so the new pipeline must meet them.
The full-text-only baseline stays below the vector variant on every quality metric except the correct-empty rate, which is the same 0.2 in both: the floor of 0.3 those runs used was a placeholder.

#226 deploys the reranked variant (hybrid pool of 30 scored by rerank-3) and switches `variant` to it with the minimums unchanged. Its floor of 0.38 and final count of 5 were calibrated on these same questions (results/reranked-calibration.json, floor 0, final count 8, swept offline), so its measured values are in-sample; the minimums are not raised to them. The deployed run meets every minimum: recall@pool 1, nDCG 0.9378, correct-empty rate 0.8.
